title: Synthetic air handlers: excess outside air in humid weather (generated by CAMBER)
summary: SYNTHETIC, generated locally by CAMBER (no download, no real building): two variable-air-volume air handlers' outdoor and return temperature and humidity, mixed and supply air, supply-air setpoint, OA damper, supply airflow, heating and cooling valves, fan status and occupancy, every 15 minutes for six weeks of a humid spring turning to early summer, as two units: one holding about 45 % outside air against its 20 % minimum in all weather, one economizing below a 65 F high limit. The first unit is ingested a second time without its airflow point.
teaches: what excess outside air costs, priced from the excess above the declared minimum only
the enthalpy path: in humid hours the outside air costs cooling even when it is cooler than the return air
economizing hours cost nothing, and the heating path in cold weather
why the estimate declines without a declared minimum or a known airflow, and how the config supplies them
publisher: CAMBER (generated locally by the user's copy)
citation: CAMBER synthetic dataset synthetic-ahu-excess-oa, generator ahu_excess_oa (camber.datasets._synthetic_ahu_excess_oa), seed 195. Generated data, not measurements from any building.
timezone: naive generated clock (no DST); 15-minute samples from 2025-04-28 (a Monday) for 42 days
equipment: 2 variable-air-volume air handlers (the first also ingested without its airflow point)

fault_types.excess_oa: a minimum OA damper position set too high: about 45 % outside air in all weather against a declared 20 % minimum

known_issues: Synthetic: generated by CAMBER's own model of two air handlers, not measured. It shows what the rule and the cost estimate see, not how a real unit behaves; never cite it as evidence about real buildings.
AHU__excess_oa_no_flow is AHU__excess_oa read without its supply airflow point, so a label score counts the one fault twice.
The weather is generated: a smooth humid spring, with no rain, no storms and no sensor faults.
